name: InterContinental Chicago Magnificent Mile
positioning: Historic 1929 former athletic club on Michigan Avenue in downtown Chicago, now a member of the Historic Hotels of America
best_for: Travelers who want a historic landmark base on the Magnificent Mile
Swimmers and families drawn to a 1920s indoor pool high above the city

facts.text: The hotel was originally built in 1929 as the men's Medinah Athletic Club.
The building became a hotel in 1944 and opened as InterContinental Chicago Magnificent Mile in March 1990.
The hotel is a member of the Historic Hotels of America.
The building keeps its original marble columns, painted ceilings, cast-bronze friezes and grand staircase.
The building was once home to secret speakeasies.
The InterContinental Spa has two treatment rooms, a couples room and two Finnish saunas.
The spa menu covers facials, body wraps and massages.
Rooms have marble bathrooms with premium bath amenities.
Select rooms and suites have city or river views.
The hotel is at 505 North Michigan Avenue in Chicago.
Michael Jordan's Steak House in the hotel serves prime, dry-aged, hand-cut beef.
Casa Chi is a Nikkei lounge by Chef Richard Sandoval that blends Japanese techniques with Peruvian flavors.

highlights.text: The historic indoor junior Olympic-size pool sits 14 stories above the Magnificent Mile.
The pool keeps its original 1920s Spanish tiles and a terra cotta Neptune fountain.
Olympic gold medalist and Tarzan actor Johnny Weissmuller trained in the pool during the Medinah Athletic Club era.
The two-story Royal and Presidential Suites have sweeping city views and spacious living areas.
The hotel's bronze doors open onto the Magnificent Mile, a 13-block stretch of venues, restaurants, bars and shopping.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the location is a high-traffic tourist area.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
